title: Back to Roots
summary: A landscape proposal told through a graphic novel, imagining cultural continuity and renewed relations with land around Lake Okeechobee.
description: Back to Roots is a speculative landscape design project presented as a graphic novel. Historical research grounds the story, while fictional characters and proposed interventions explore how a landscape marked by displacement might be transformed into a place that sustains memory and cultural continuity.

The comic follows Osceola, a fictional Seminole elder, as he revisits memories of his grandmother and childhood. His story connects the loss of home and language with changing relationships to land and water. In conversation with landscape architect Allison, these memories become the starting point for a proposed preserve, where planting, gathering, and the changing forest allow people to encounter different layers of history.

Within the existing forest, the preserve brings together a memorial garden, an experimental planting field, and a medicine wheel garden. Annual digging and flooding would expose the ground and cause trees to die, giving material form to displacement. Fallen trees would then become compost for cultivated plants. This uneasy cycle places an expression of loss alongside the possibility of renewal, connecting remembrance with the ongoing practice and transmission of plant knowledge.

Through collage, dialogue, maps, and successive landscape scenes, the book makes time part of the design. Its final chapter extends the imagined initiative into landscapes shaped by sugarcane cultivation, while leaving its economic consequences unresolved. Back to Roots asks how cultural continuity might be sustained within a changing landscape, and what responsibilities arise when remembrance becomes a continuing practice of care.
